## :x: BLOCKING REVIEW / not ready for approval yet.

Review record: PR #372 / Issue #371
Exact head: `f76fbfdab8bd0a21845962ac8bf886aa525db970`
Declared base: `release/0.1.0-r2`
Review timestamp: 2026-08-19T20:16:44Z

### 1. Issue and evidence fully inspected
Read the complete Issue and inspect all evidence before judging the implementation.

- [x] The complete canonical Issue was read, including body, acceptance criteria, comments, links, and dependencies.
  > Read Issue #371 via REST, including its full problem statement, architecture constraints, eight acceptance criteria, verification guidance, and relationship to merged PR #362/#360; the Issue has zero comments, no attachment URLs, and its timeline links the implementation commits and follow-up Issue #374.
- [x] Every Issue attachment or linked evidence artifact was inspected, including screenshots, videos, and comparison references.
  > Issue #371 contains no Markdown links, external URLs, screenshots, videos, or attachment references; I verified that directly and inspected its linked predecessor context by reading Issue #360, its comment, and merged PR #362's browser-evidence description and merge metadata.
- [x] Related Issues, parent/ancestor PRs, and existing accepted behavior were inspected where relevant.
  > I inspected the relevant predecessor Issue #360, merged parent PR #362 at b6472908, its exact-head reviewer history, and #371's timeline; #362's approved browser contracts are the creditable existing behavior, while the open follow-up #374 is explicitly downstream architecture context rather than a dependency for this bounded fix.

### 2. Issue intent, scope, and protected behavior understood
Identify the user problem and intended observable behavior independently of the PR description.

- [x] The user problem and desired observable behavior were stated independently of the PR implementation.
  > The Issue independently defines the defect as a folder/FileManager-to-Desktop drop whose resource moves but lands at an unrelated default slot; the desired behavior is a same-NodeId move through filesystem authority with committed icon/name placement tracking the actual release ghost, subject only to Desktop bounds/collision policy.
- [x] Protected behavior, explicit non-goals, and compatibility boundaries were identified.
  > The protected boundaries are explicit: Desktop owns NodeId-keyed placement and reconciliation, FileManager owns drag orchestration, FsService performs the directory move, and the preview stays presentation-only; the follow-up must preserve #360 cross-window targeting and must not add filename hacks or a second filesystem/drop authority.
- [x] The PR scope matches the Issue intent rather than a narrower or implementation-defined substitute.
  > The exact diff is limited to the incoming-placement adapter, Desktop reconciliation/persistence, two focused model tests, one packaged-browser regression, and the Desktop authority documentation; it implements the Issue's folder-to-Desktop handoff rather than changing filesystem mutation or unrelated drag behavior.

### 3. Release policy and integration context verified
Check release-specific authority, declared bases, stacked dependencies, and which parent work is actually creditable.

- [x] Current assignment, release policy, target branch, and package/version constraints were read.
  > Read r2 SPECIFIC-REVIEW policy plus Plasmon AGENTS/TESTING guidance: target is release/0.1.0-r2, package identity is frozen at Plasmon v0.1.0/neutron.json version 100, and required lanes are kernel, Fast Bun tests, packaged smoke, packaged Playwright specialist acceptance, and browser persistence; PR metadata confirms that declared base and exact head.
- [x] The declared PR base, stacked-parent relationship, and integration assumptions were verified.
  > PR #372 declares release/0.1.0-r2 as its base and has no stacked predecessor; GitHub comparison reports merge base 2c0346ac, the merged PR #362 merge commit, with 9 issue-371 commits ahead and zero behind, so #362 behavior is integrated and creditable.
- [x] Only merged or otherwise explicitly creditable parent behavior was counted as implemented.
  > The only parent behavior relied upon is PR #362, which GitHub records as MERGED into release/0.1.0-r2 at 2c0346ac; the comparison for #372 starts from that merge base, so no unmerged ancestor or speculative future Issue #374 behavior was counted.

### 4. Implementation correctness and failure paths verified
Review success, failure, boundary, asynchronous, cancellation, cleanup, and regression behavior—not only the happy path.

- [x] Success, failure, empty, exceptional, and boundary paths were inspected where applicable.
  > Inspected exact-head Desktop reconciliation and pointer-adapter paths: free/clamped/colliding incoming proposals, no candidate/invalid target, operation-busy handling, FsService move failure cleanup and refresh, pointer cancel/Escape, unmount cleanup, and the one-frame preview teardown after successful refresh.
- [ ] Async ownership, cancellation, teardown, cleanup, error visibility, and resource ownership were inspected where applicable.
  > :x: Desktop.tsx invokes persistDesktopPositions() from onIncomingDropPlacement without awaiting or returning its promise, while the pointer adapter proceeds with FsService.move(); a metadata-write failure is only surfaced asynchronously via setError and cannot prevent the move or trigger a retry, leaving the committed placement non-durable. The same pre-move callback also records placement when operationState.begin() rejects or a later move partially fails.
- [x] The change does not materially regress unrelated accepted behavior.
  > The exact-head packaged specialist run passed all four existing #360 drag journeys (Desktop reposition, cross-window folder move, target transitions/cleanup, and grouped move); the diff preserves the existing entry-hit branch and only adds a distinct surface candidate path, so no unrelated accepted regression is evidenced.

### 5. Architecture, authority, and subsystem boundaries preserved
Confirm that behavior remains in the canonical owning layer and does not create parallel authority or cross a product boundary.

- [x] The canonical owning service, model, controller, or adapter remains authoritative.
  > The exact code keeps FsService/validateDirectoryDrop/moveNodesToDirectory as filesystem and directory-drop authority, the pointer adapter as browser geometry/orchestration, and layout.ts plus Desktop.tsx as the sole NodeId-keyed placement/reconciliation/persistence authority; no second filesystem store or preview-owned coordinates were introduced.
- [x] Relevant identity, filesystem, Neutron, Process, Windowing, Shell, security, or other subsystem boundaries remain intact.
  > The handoff carries stable NodeIds and target directory NodeId through the existing FileManager DOM boundary, then validates/stats and mutates through FsService; the change does not touch Neutron, Process, Windowing, Shell, security, or package identity boundaries.
- [x] No duplicate authority, hidden parallel implementation, or convenience architecture was introduced.
  > drop-placement.ts is explicitly a translation/event adapter only; its target-relative points are accepted and reconciled solely by Desktop.layout.ts, while directory validation and FsService mutation remain in the shared pointer adapter path, so no parallel placement or filesystem authority was added.

### 6. Tests are honest, deterministic, and sufficient
Tests must observe production behavior at the lowest truthful layer and must not be weakened or made circular.

- [x] Tests assert user-visible or contract behavior rather than source shape, incidental structure, or constants alone.
  > The Bun tests call production incomingDropPlacementIntent/applyIncomingDesktopDropPositions and assert translated coordinates, stable IDs, free placement, bounds clamping, and incumbent collision behavior; the Playwright test drives real pointer input and observes rendered ghost, canonical target, source removal, and committed entry geometry rather than source strings.
- [x] Tests use the lowest honest layer with deterministic control and appropriate negative/boundary cases.
  > The placement translation is covered deterministically in Bun, while real pointer hit-testing and rendered continuity remain in Playwright; deterministic cases include grouped relative geometry, canonical workspace clamping, and incumbent collision protection, with existing #360 browser tests covering invalid-target/cancel cleanup.
- [x] Fixtures, examples, tolerances, and bounds match the Issue rather than being relaxed to fit the implementation.
  > The browser tolerance is 4px, matching the established #360 release-continuity guard, and the unit clamp expectation uses the production 92x88 Desktop entry dimensions (800−92, 600−88); candidate points avoid existing entries with a safety margin rather than weakening the post-drop assertion.

### 7. Runtime, packaged, browser, and manual evidence verified
Use real packaged/browser/manual evidence whenever the claim depends on layout, assets, runtime, persistence, or visual parity.

- [x] The required evidence layer for the Issue was identified correctly.
  > Issue #371 explicitly requires Bun/headless for placement handoff semantics and bounded packaged Playwright for pointer capture, hit testing, and rendered ghost/committed geometry; the PR supplies both focused Bun tests and a real installed-browser spec under test/e2e.
- [ ] Packaged, browser, runtime, persistence, or human/manual evidence was inspected where the claim requires it.
  > :x: Exact-head packaged job 95976262187 reports the new #371 browser test failing at line 109 after a 20-second wait because the source NodeId remained in Documents; only retry #1 passed. The required real-browser evidence is therefore flaky rather than a deterministic successful packaged regression.
- [x] Execution evidence is distinguished from CI status and is not replaced by a green status label.
  > I treated CI as evidence metadata, not proof: `gh pr checks` shows Fast, kernel, smoke, and persistence passing but the required specialist lane and flake summary failing; the specialist log supplies the concrete first-attempt source-retention failure and retry result.

### 8. Compatibility, regressions, documentation, and release obligations reviewed
Check durable state, compatibility, scope, documentation, generated artifacts, and applicable release obligations.

- [x] Durable state, persistence, migration, serialized contracts, and upgrade/restart behavior were reviewed where applicable.
  > The diff keeps the existing `plasmon.desktop.positions.v1` NodeId-keyed metadata contract and adds no schema, migration, manifest, or release-package changes; I traced readDesktopPositions/persistDesktopPositions and verified the durable-state boundary, while the unowned incoming write failure is recorded separately as a correctness blocker.
- [x] Required architecture, API, developer-facing, persistence, or integration documentation was reviewed or updated where applicable.
  > The PR updates desktop/README.md with the incoming target-relative proposal and authority boundary, and I reviewed the existing file-manager README’s adapter/authority documentation; the changed-file list contains no schema, package, or undocumented public-contract expansion.
- [x] Scope, generated artifacts, dependency changes, release obligations, and unrelated work were reviewed.
  > The exact compare contains only nine scoped Desktop/FileManager source, test, browser-spec, and README files; no package manifests, lockfiles, generated archives, build output, dependencies, or version changes are included, and r2 policy correctly requires no version bump.

### 9. Exact-head and reviewer-operational disposition verified
The formal disposition must be bound to the current exact head and must follow reviewer independence and reporting rules.

- [x] The exact PR head and declared base were recorded and refreshed immediately before output.
  > Fresh gh metadata records PR #372 OPEN at head f76fbfdab8bd0a21845962ac8bf886aa525db970 with declared base release/0.1.0-r2, and github-check.sh --json still classifies that exact head as REVIEW with the specialist check FAILED.
- [x] The reviewer did not implement product changes, merge, force-push, or alter another agent's work.
  > The reviewer made no product edits or GitHub mutations: the worktree retains only its pre-existing executable-bit change in packages/neutron-cli/src/index.ts, and this review used read-only API/diff/log inspection without merge, push, force-push, or branch alteration.
- [x] CI status and failures are recorded as merge/infrastructure evidence, not used as product-correctness proof.
  > CI is recorded separately from code claims: the Fast/kernel/smoke/persistence lanes passed, while both the specialist job and Flake probe 2 failed on the same #371 source-retention assertion; I classify this as unresolved browser/test nondeterminism relevant to the acceptance gate, not as proof that all product behavior is incorrect.

### 10. Acceptance criteria represented in production code and tests
Every Issue acceptance criterion must have production implementation and at least one honest executable test in this PR or an already-merged or pending-merge parent branch. Each criterion below comes directly from the linked Issue.

- [x] Dragging a resource from a non-Desktop Explorer/FileManager into a free Desktop location moves the same NodeId into `/Desktop`.
  > The production pointer adapter performs canonical directory validation and FsService move for stable source IDs, and the real-browser regression observes the same ID leaving Documents and appearing in Desktop; all three preceding criterion checks are satisfied, although the exact-head run remains flaky as recorded under runtime evidence.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > Production pointer-up code resolves the canonical directory target, retains the stable source NodeIds, and calls moveNodesToDirectory(fs, source, target), while the Desktop callback handles placement intent separately; the browser spec exercises a real Documents source into the Desktop directory.
    - [x] An executable test covers it.
      > test/e2e/plasmon-drag-placement-371.spec.ts creates a real Documents file, captures its NodeId, requires the Desktop directory NodeId as target, releases the pointer, and asserts the source count reaches zero and the same NodeId appears on Desktop.
    - [x] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > The browser regression uses semantic locators plus real page.mouse down/move/up and NodeId DOM assertions; it does not inspect implementation names, callback wiring, or internal constants to claim the cross-surface move.

- [x] The committed Desktop entry appears at approximately the drag ghost/release location rather than an unrelated default slot.
  > Production translation plus Desktop canonical reconciliation is exercised by deterministic unit cases, and the real-browser test directly compares pre-release ghost and post-release entry rectangles; the criterion is represented honestly, with the separate flaky-run blocker still unresolved.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > incomingDropPlacementIntent translates the source entry rectangle plus the exact pointer delta into the target surface coordinate system, and Desktop applies that proposal before canonical clamp/collision reconciliation instead of allocating the unrelated first-free slot.
    - [x] An executable test covers it.
      > The packaged test records the final ghost bounding box before release, waits for the committed same-NodeId Desktop entry, and compares x/y within 4px; the Bun placement test separately protects free proposals against default-slot replacement.
    - [x] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > The regression observes real browser geometry with boundingBox() before and after page.mouse release and asserts rendered same-NodeId placement; it does not inspect applyIncomingDesktopDropPositions or compare source text.

- [ ] Pointer-to-entry grab offset remains preserved across the cross-FileManager drop.
  > :x: The criterion is not fully covered: although production reuses the source rectangle plus pointer delta, the new cross-FileManager browser journey records a non-centered grab without asserting its offset against the ghost/release coordinates. The only direct offset assertion is the merged #360 Desktop-to-Desktop test, so this new direction lacks criterion-level executable protection.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > The drag state captures the source rectangle and pointer start, computes dx/dy from the same pointer coordinates, and translates the preview/source rectangle without re-anchoring; the incoming placement uses that same delta and source rectangle.
    - [ ] An executable test covers it.
      > :x: The new cross-FileManager browser test uses a non-centered grab but never asserts pointer-to-entry offset (for example, release pointer minus ghost top-left equals the initial grab delta). Its only geometry assertion is committed Desktop versus preview. Merged #362 tests this offset for Desktop-to-Desktop, not for the new Explorer-to-Desktop handoff, and the Bun translation test does not model pointer coordinates.
    - [x] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > The test uses real page.mouse input, rendered bounding boxes, semantic NodeId locators, and the committed entry, so its assertions are behavioral rather than source-shape checks; the specific missing offset assertion is recorded under the preceding coverage checkbox.

- [x] Any final position adjustment is attributable only to canonical Desktop bounds/collision policy.
  > The production path clamps incoming geometry and delegates all remaining adjustment to the canonical reconciliation policy, and deterministic tests protect free, bounds, and incumbent-collision outcomes; no unrelated adjustment source is present.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > applyIncomingDesktopDropPositions first clamps each proposed point to workspace limits, then delegates exclusively to reconcileDesktopPositions, whose only further changes are incumbent-preserving overlap resolution and deterministic bounded fallback; no filename or pointer-specific adjustment exists.
    - [x] An executable test covers it.
      > drop-placement.test.ts covers a free proposal staying exact, an out-of-bounds proposal clamping to 708/512 from the production 92x88 dimensions, and an incoming proposal colliding with an incumbent being relocated rather than stealing it.
    - [x] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > The tests call the real placement function and assert resulting NodeId-keyed coordinates and collision outcomes; they do not inspect implementation branches or merely assert constants.

- [x] Existing Desktop-to-Desktop reposition behavior from #360 remains unchanged.
  > The shared pointer adapter preserves the existing same-parent rejection/reposition branch, and the merged #360 browser contract still passes on this head with real ghost offset, continuity, and cleanup assertions.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > The existing Desktop branch still sends same-parent drops through validateDirectoryDrop, which rejects already-parented entries, and then calls onDesktopReposition with the original ids, delta, and bounds; exact-head packaged #360 reposition, continuity, and cancel tests all passed.
    - [x] An executable test covers it.
      > Merged #362’s executable packaged suite remains in the specialist run and passed its Desktop ghost/reposition continuity test at line 185, covering real pointer movement, committed geometry, and cancel cleanup for the preserved Desktop-to-Desktop path.
    - [x] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.

### 6. Tests are honest, deterministic, and sufficient
Tests must observe production behavior at the lowest truthful layer and must not be weakened or made circular.

- [ ] Tests assert user-visible or contract behavior rather than source shape, incidental structure, or constants alone.
  > :x: The registry is a machine-readable contract with objective criteria, but PR #386 adds no executable regression test and the exact-head tree contains no test referring to `documentation-boundaries.json`. `apps/plasmon/package.json` runs existing model/UI suites only; the passing Fast Bun check therefore does not parse or validate this registry. Add focused production/repository test coverage or provide an already-merged test that proves the registry’s contract.
- [ ] Tests use the lowest honest layer with deterministic control and appropriate negative/boundary cases.
  > :x: This is pure filesystem/JSON policy and should be covered deterministically without browser or packaged layers, but the PR has no test file and no executable consumer of the registry. Consequently there is no negative coverage for missing/inherited ownership, retired paths, empty discovery roots, or the `shared` exemption; those cases are deferred to Issue #382 rather than proven for this registry.
- [x] Fixtures, examples, tolerances, and bounds match the Issue rather than being relaxed to fit the implementation.
  > No test fixtures, timing tolerances, generated examples, or relaxed numeric bounds were added. The only explicit exception is `src/native-apps/shared` in `nonBoundaryChildren`, matching the Issue’s requirement not to force documentation into implementation-detail roots; the separate omission of the nested Monaco boundary is an inventory-accuracy defect, not a fixture or tolerance issue.

### 7. Runtime, packaged, browser, and manual evidence verified
Use real packaged/browser/manual evidence whenever the claim depends on layout, assets, runtime, persistence, or visual parity.

- [x] The required evidence layer for the Issue was identified correctly.
  > Issue #381 is declarative filesystem/JSON documentation work, so the truthful evidence layer is JSON parsing plus deterministic repository-tree validation; it does not require browser, package, Neutron, or visual evidence. `apps/plasmon/TESTING.md` confirms pure deterministic policy belongs in focused tests, while packaged checks are for installed/runtime claims.
- [x] Packaged, browser, runtime, persistence, or human/manual evidence was inspected where the claim requires it.
  > No packaged, browser, persistence, Neutron-runtime, or visual behavior is claimed: the changed files are only a docs README and JSON inventory, and Issue #381 has no manual/browser acceptance criterion. The passing packaged checks are incidental release evidence, not required proof for this declarative registry.
- [ ] Execution evidence is distinguished from CI status and is not replaced by a green status label.
  > :x: The PR’s Validation section only asserts manual reconciliation and the branch’s two-file scope; it gives no command or execution output for parsing/checking the registry. The green Fast Bun and packaged CI jobs run unchanged suites and do not reference `documentation-boundaries.json`, so they cannot prove the registry accuracy—especially with `shared/monaco` omitted.

### 8. Compatibility, regressions, documentation, and release obligations reviewed
Check durable state, compatibility, scope, documentation, generated artifacts, and applicable release obligations.

- [x] Durable state, persistence, migration, serialized contracts, and upgrade/restart behavior were reviewed where applicable.
  > The PR changes no application memory root, persistence API, package manifest, migration, or runtime serialization contract; it adds a repository documentation JSON file with a versioned metadata label only. Therefore production upgrade/restart and durable-user-state obligations are not applicable.
- [x] Required architecture, API, developer-facing, persistence, or integration documentation was reviewed or updated where applicable.
  > The required developer-facing documentation update is present: `apps/plasmon/docs/README.md` links `documentation-boundaries.json` and identifies it as the single inventory source, while the registry records local versus inherited AGENTS ownership. The registry’s missing Monaco entry is an accuracy defect in that documentation, not an absence of the required documentation update.
- [x] Scope, generated artifacts, dependency changes, release obligations, and unrelated work were reviewed.
  > PR metadata and the complete diff show only the intended docs README and new JSON registry; there are no dependency, package/version, generated build, lockfile, or unrelated product changes. The three commits remain narrowly scoped to defining and pointing at the registry.

### 9. Exact-head and reviewer-operational disposition verified
The formal disposition must be bound to the current exact head and must follow reviewer independence and reporting rules.

- [x] The exact PR head and declared base were recorded and refreshed immediately before output.
  > Refreshed GitHub immediately before this answer: PR #386 is OPEN at exact head `383c2dc7a01034bb60c339e4cd0f654a7933e623`, base `release/0.1.0-r2`, and the reviewer queue reports the same ACTION REVIEW candidate. The earlier relative-script probe failed only because it ran from the repo instead of reviewer root; the absolute reviewer helper succeeded.
- [x] The reviewer did not implement product changes, merge, force-push, or alter another agent's work.
  > Only read-only GitHub/API/tree inspection and temporary `/tmp` artifacts were used; no product files were edited, committed, merged, force-pushed, or pushed. The reviewer worktree still shows only the pre-existing mode change on `packages/neutron-cli/src/index.ts`, which is unrelated to PR #386 and was left untouched.
- [x] CI status and failures are recorded as merge/infrastructure evidence, not used as product-correctness proof.
  > The current checks were recorded separately from correctness: Fast Bun and all three packaged gates pass, while `kernel` is skipped with a passing applicability determination. The review has not treated those statuses as proof of registry accuracy; the missing registry test and omitted Monaco boundary remain independently blocking findings.

### 10. Acceptance criteria represented in production code and tests
Every Issue acceptance criterion must have production implementation and at least one honest executable test in this PR or an already-merged or pending-merge parent branch. Each criterion below comes directly from the linked Issue.

- [ ] There is one repository-owned machine-readable boundary registry.
  > :x: The registry file itself is present, but the criterion is not fully evidenced: PR #386 adds no executable test and therefore has no behavior-level observation of uniqueness or machine-readable validity. The current passing CI runs do not consume `apps/plasmon/docs/documentation-boundaries.json`.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > The exact head contains the repository-owned file `apps/plasmon/docs/documentation-boundaries.json` (GitHub reports it as a committed 6,211-byte file), with schema `plasmon-documentation-boundaries-v1` and a boundaries array. For this documentation artifact criterion, the registry itself is the production repository representation; no runtime feature code is required.
    - [ ] An executable test covers it.
      > :x: PR #386 changes zero test files, and repository code search finds no executable test referencing the new registry. Issue #382 is still open and cannot be counted as merged coverage, so the existence of this machine-readable contract is currently guarded only by review prose and CI suites that do not consume it.
    - [ ] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > :x: No executable test exists in the PR to observe registry behavior at all, so none can demonstrate behavior rather than merely inspect source shape. A focused parser/tree-contract test must load the JSON and assert its observable boundary inventory semantics.

- [ ] Every currently required README/AGENTS boundary is represented accurately.
  > :x: The registry contains 32 declared paths, but exact-head inspection found at least one explicit documentation boundary (`src/native-apps/shared/monaco`) outside those 32 and no executable test to detect the mismatch. The criterion therefore fails both accuracy evidence and behavior-level test coverage.
    - [ ] Production code represents the behavior.
      > :x: Exact-head tree comparison shows `apps/plasmon/src/native-apps/shared/monaco` has both README.md and AGENTS.md but is absent from the registry; its AGENTS file explicitly defines that directory as a browser/editor adapter boundary. `apps/plasmon/src/demo` also has a README but is unregistered. Thus the committed registry does not accurately represent every existing documentation boundary.
    - [ ] An executable test covers it.
      > :x: The PR adds no `.test.ts`/`.test.tsx` file and repository code search finds no test consuming the registry. Issue #382’s future validator tests are still open, so there is no executable coverage proving existing README/AGENTS paths—including the omitted Monaco boundary—are represented accurately.
    - [ ] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > :x: Because no executable test was added or found, there is no behavior-level observation of filesystem ownership or inheritance; the only evidence is the registry source itself. A test must enumerate the exact tree and assert boundary semantics rather than merely checking JSON text or constants.

- [ ] Inherited AGENTS ownership is explicit rather than implied by an external document.
  > :x: The registry explicitly stores inherited `from` paths for 14 entries, but no test resolves or validates them. The criterion’s representation exists, yet the PR provides no executable evidence that the declared inheritance is valid rather than merely source-shaped metadata.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > The registry encodes inherited ownership as structured data, with 15 entries carrying `agents: { mode: "inherited", from: ... }`; examples include Sharing from `src/os/AGENTS.md` and EmulatorJS/js-dos/native apps from `src/native-apps/AGENTS.md`. This is the requested repository representation, although the omitted Monaco boundary remains a separate completeness defect.
    - [ ] An executable test covers it.
      > :x: No executable test in PR #386 or the existing exact-head search exercises the `agents.mode = "inherited"` entries or verifies their `from` paths. The structured fields are present, but they are not behaviorally guarded against omission or invalid ownership.
    - [ ] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > :x: The JSON has explicit `from` strings, but with no executable consumer/test there is no observation that inherited ownership resolves to the actual ancestor files. A behavior-level test must resolve these three declared source paths and reject missing or non-ancestor ownership, rather than only inspecting JSON keys.

- [ ] Current Sharing and EmulatorJS documentation ownership is explicitly dispositioned.
  > :x: Both Sharing and EmulatorJS are represented as records, but the criterion is not fully evidenced because no executable test consumes the registry or resolves their README/AGENTS ownership. Existing product tests cannot substitute for registry-specific behavior coverage.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > The exact registry has explicit entries for both required boundaries: `src/os/sharing` is an `os-subsystem` with local README and inherited `src/os/AGENTS.md`, while `src/native-apps/emulatorjs` is a `runtime-host` with local README and inherited `src/native-apps/AGENTS.md`.
    - [ ] An executable test covers it.
      > :x: Although the JSON contains Sharing and EmulatorJS entries, PR #386 adds no executable test for either disposition. The passing existing Sharing/EmulatorJS product tests do not load this registry, so they cannot detect a missing or incorrect documentation ownership entry.
    - [ ] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > :x: No test observes actual ownership resolution for either path; the only evidence is the two JSON records themselves. A registry contract test must verify local README presence and inherited AGENTS resolution for Sharing and EmulatorJS, rather than treating source literals as behavior.

- [ ] Retired `src/platform/` and `src/gui2/` are absent from active boundaries.
  > :x: The exact registry excludes both retired paths, but PR #386 provides no executable test or behavior-level observation to preserve that exclusion. The criterion is source-present yet unguarded against future registry drift.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > Enumerating all 32 registry paths at the exact head finds no `apps/plasmon/src/platform` or `apps/plasmon/src/gui2` entry. The committed registry therefore represents the required exclusion of both retired boundaries.
    - [ ] An executable test covers it.
      > :x: No executable test asserts that retired `src/platform/` and `src/gui2/` remain absent. The absence is visible in the JSON source, but the PR adds no registry contract test to guard against either path being reintroduced.
    - [ ] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > :x: There is no behavior-level test for the retired-path exclusion; only a source grep of the registry can show the current absence. A deterministic registry test should assert the active boundary set excludes both retired paths.

- [ ] Discovery roots are defined so a new first-class `src/os/*` or `src/native-apps/*` directory must be classified.
  > :x: The two discovery roots and `shared` exemption are present as declarative records, but the PR supplies no executable test or consumer proving the promised “must be classified” behavior. That observable enforcement is explicitly deferred to open Issue #382.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > The registry defines both requested discovery roots with `children: "directories"`: `apps/plasmon/src/os` has no exemptions, and `apps/plasmon/src/native-apps` explicitly exempts only `shared`. This is the declarative production representation; enforcement of new children is intentionally deferred to Issue #382.
    - [ ] An executable test covers it.
      > :x: The two discovery-root records exist, but no executable test creates or inspects representative new child directories and asserts that unclassified children are rejected. That enforcement test is absent from PR #386 and only planned in open Issue #382.
    - [ ] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > :x: The discovery-root behavior is only encoded as JSON strings/arrays; no test walks or models a new child to observe classification failure. In particular, no executable evidence verifies that `shared` is the only intentional native-app exemption or that a new `src/os` child cannot silently escape.

- [ ] The registry does not force README/AGENTS files into implementation-detail directories.
  > :x: The `shared` exemption is declared and appropriately avoids a fake root boundary, but no executable test observes that behavior. The criterion therefore lacks the required behavior-level proof, and the registry simultaneously misses the nested `shared/monaco` boundary.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > The registry explicitly marks `shared` as the sole `src/native-apps` non-boundary child, so the discovery-root contract will not demand a README/AGENTS pair for the shared implementation root itself. This matches the Issue’s no-fake-boundary goal; the separate failure is that the nested real `shared/monaco` boundary is omitted rather than forcibly documented.
    - [ ] An executable test covers it.
      > :x: No executable test verifies the `nonBoundaryChildren: ["shared"]` exemption or checks that implementation-detail directories are not treated as required documentation boundaries. The exception is present in JSON but unguarded against accidental removal or expansion.
    - [ ] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > :x: The only evidence is the literal `shared` exemption; no test exercises a tree containing implementation-only children and observes that they remain exempt. Source inspection cannot prove the future discovery behavior this criterion promises.

- [ ] `apps/plasmon/docs/README.md` identifies the registry as the source for documentation-boundary inventory.
  > :x: The README correctly names and links the registry, but the criterion is not fully evidenced because the PR adds no executable test that observes this documentation-source contract. The complete changed-file list contains only the README and JSON registry.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > The exact README states: “The machine-readable boundary inventory is `documentation-boundaries.json`” and calls it “the single source” for directory boundaries, README/AGENTS mode, and discovery-root classification. This directly satisfies the requested documentation pointer.
    - [ ] An executable test covers it.
      > :x: No executable test checks that the docs map points to the registry or preserves the single-source wording. The README edit is present, but it is unguarded documentation text and the PR changes no test file.
    - [ ] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > :x: The README contains the expected link and wording, but no executable test observes or validates that link/authority contract. A source grep is not a behavior-level test, and PR #386 adds no docs-contract test.

### Summary
> Approval is allowed only when every checkbox above is checked. CI status is recorded separately and is not used as proof that the Issue is solved.
